edition: Friedenthal, Miller, Sexton, Hershkoff, Steinman & McKenzie, Civil Procedure, 13th ed. (2022)
basis: The supplied four-page syllabus, 726-page casebook PDF, and nineteen-page Mallory excerpt. Course-wide page spans also retain surrounding context; exact named assignments and full-chapter instructions remain visible.

weeks.title: The civil action and the territorial starting point
weeks.instructions: Read printed pages 1–29, Capron, Tickle, Pennoyer, and Article III §§ 1–2. The syllabus places the first overview before the first class. The additional pages here include the assigned case accounts and their immediate discussion.

weeks.title: From territorial presence to minimum contacts
weeks.instructions: Hess, International Shoe, McGee, Hanson, and Gray. The casebook’s notes supply the surrounding development.

weeks.title: Purposeful activity, products, and claim-linked jurisdiction
weeks.instructions: World-Wide Volkswagen, Keeton, Calder, Kulko, Burger King, Asahi, Nicastro, Walden, and Bristol-Myers Squibb. Bristol-Myers appears later in the book and is included separately.

weeks.title: Relatedness, general jurisdiction, consent, and property
weeks.instructions: Ford; Goodyear and its discussion of Perkins (Benguet) and Helicopteros; Daimler; BNSF; Insurance Corp. of Ireland; Bremen; Carnival Cruise; Zippo; Shaffer; Burnham; and the separate Mallory PDF, printed supplement pages 422–440.

weeks.title: Notice, service, and an opportunity to be heard
weeks.instructions: Study Mullane carefully. Read the service discussion, Szukhent, Wyman, Sniadach, Fuentes, Doehr, and printed pages 278–296 with care. The syllabus separately assigns Federal Rules 4 and 12 in the supplement.

weeks.title: Subject-matter jurisdiction and diversity
weeks.instructions: Lacks, Article III, Strawbridge, § 1332, Mas v. Perry, and A.F.A. Tours. Read the statutes identified in the chapter, especially §§ 1331, 1332, 1367, and 1441. Subject-matter jurisdiction recurs later in the course.

weeks.title: Federal questions, supplemental jurisdiction, and removal
weeks.instructions: Federal-question jurisdiction and § 1331; Mottley, American Well Works, Shoshone, Smith, Grable, Gunn; Gibbs, Aldinger, Kroger, Finley, § 1367, Exxon; removal and § 1441, Shamrock Oil, Home Depot, Bright v. Bechtel, Lively v. Wild Oats, and Dart Cherokee.

weeks.title: Venue, transfer, and forum non conveniens
weeks.instructions: The syllabus moves quickly through Chapter 5 and names Reasor-Hill, Bates, Livingston, Hoffman, and Piper Aircraft. Read §§ 1391, 1404, 1406, and 1407. Atlantic Marine and other chapter discussion remain available as context.

weeks.title: Erie and the law applied in federal court
weeks.instructions: Erie, Swift and Black & White Taxicab as discussed in Erie, York, Ragan, Woods, Cohen, Byrd, Hanna, and Sibbach.

weeks.title: Completing governing law; beginning modern pleading
weeks.instructions: Walker, Stewart, federal common law, Dice, the separately assigned Berk PDF, Shady Grove, and Gasperini. Begin Gillispie, Dioguardi, Conley, and Swierkiewicz. Berk v. Choy is on file (added-sources/Berk v Choy.pdf) and has its own entry.

weeks.title: Modern pleading: the entire chapter
weeks.instructions: Read all of Chapter 8, including the material not assigned for formal case presentation. Named cases are Twombly, Iqbal, Tellabs, Ziervogel, Garcia, Krupski, and Surowitz. Pay close attention to Rules 8, 9, 11, 12, and 15 in the supplement.

weeks.title: Joinder and the assigned class-action chapter
weeks.instructions: Read the entirety of Chapters 9 and 10. This week emphasizes joinder; the next emphasizes class actions. Examine the governing joinder and class-action Rules and §§ 1332(d), 1407, and 1453. Interpleader and intervention remain assigned reading although no classroom time is allocated to them.

weeks.title: Class actions and multidistrict litigation
weeks.instructions: Rule 23, Hansberry, Wal-Mart, Amchem, Ortiz, Phillips Petroleum v. Shutts, Mussat, and TransUnion; introduction to multidistrict litigation. The entire chapter remains part of the preceding reading assignment.

weeks.title: Summary judgment
weeks.instructions: Focus on summary judgment, the separately named Cross reading, Celotex, and the notes on Anderson and Matsushita. Read Rule 56 and the note cases on printed pages 1031–1036 carefully. The syllabus expressly excludes the dismissal/default material on pages 1036–1046. Cross was not identified in the supplied readings; it remains a visible gap.

review: Source-based study accounts and editorial connections. No lecture record, external supplementation, current-law audit, or citator review is represented. Source-limited notes have six labeled sections but identify the details the note omits.
scopeLimits: The syllabus is a weekly guide; actual classroom announcements can supersede it.
All named readings are linked to a case account or a source file on hand.
All separately authored case accounts are indexed by explained topics. The inventory also preserves table-of-cases references in mapped reading spans without pretending each has a full brief.
Berk v. Choy and Cross v. United States are full entries with the opinions on file (added-sources); the 2026–2027 supplement (354 pages) is on file and every provision guide opens its page.
The supplied casebook records law and commentary at its publication. Mallory is a later supplied excerpt. No other updates have been imported.
Chapter 8, Chapter 9, and Chapter 10 are included in full. Interpleader and intervention remain included despite no allocated classroom time.
The end of printed page 1036 begins excluded dismissal material; the full source remains viewable, but that section is not added to the summary-judgment assignment.
